newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed sharply down on Wednesday at an intraday low of 8.2950 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based China foreign exchange market due to intervention by the People's Bank of China, traders said.
The close last Thursday, the last trading day before the Chinese new year holiday, was 8.2918. The market has been closed since Friday for the annual five-day break.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2916 and hit an intraday high of 8.2908 early in the session. It then moved in a narrow range of 8.2915 and 8.2920 for most of the session, traders said.
The central bank sold the yuan in the last 15 minutes of trading to depress the local currency, they said.
Trading was dull as the holiday mood prevailed, with most transactions done at 8.2918, traders said.
One dealer said reduced demand for the local currency right after the holiday was another factor in its fall.
"The demand for the yuan was light right after the holiday, helping depress it," he said.
A second dealer characterised the yuan's fall as very sharp but he said that as a result it would probably rebound in the next few days.
"Thin volume made price movements much easier and exceptionally wide today," he said.
"The yuan is likely to regain ground and consolidate around the 8.2920 level on Thursday due to the market's strong pro-yuan sentiment," he said.
The yuan closed up slightly at 6.6788 from 6.6900 against 100 Japanese yen, and down at an intraday low of 1.0709 from 1.0680 against the Hong Kong dollar.
